subject: Ephemeral log eviction protocol and cross-border purge timeline
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@logicacloud.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Ephemeral log eviction protocol and cross-border purge timeline

Hi Sofia —

Quick intro: we're working through a narrow purge window for ephemeral request logs for EU customers that will impact how long KV-caches and ephemeral traces are retained by your systems (and any subprocessors). We need to confirm a few items before finalizing Redwood's guidance to customers:

- Full subprocessor list for any backup or snapshot systems that may receive ephemeral logs (CloudStore, BlobKeep, etc.).
- Whether backups are restored automatically after a deletion/eviction run.
- Proposed rolling purge window: target Aug 6–8 (UTC) but flexible if you have maintenance constraints.

I've attached a short proposal (retention-eviction-proposal-v2.pdf) and a retention matrix with the delta we need for EU DPA carveouts (retention-matrix.xlsx). Can you confirm by COB Monday your subprocessor posture and whether you can provide SOC2-type evidence for the backup subprocessors?

If there are cross-border copies we also need to list where those copies live and whether there are longer-term logs kept for forensic hold.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@logicacloud.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 11:04:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Ephemeral log eviction protocol and cross-border purge timeline

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. We reviewed internally and here's what we can share immediately:

- Subprocessors: we use CloudStore (EU-west), BackupLedger (global, hosted in us-central), and an archival partner, GlacierEdge, for long-term snapshots.
- Backups: standard behavior is immutable snapshots every 24 hours; these are not auto-restored by default. Restores require a manual ticket and are logged.
- SOC2 evidence: we can provide recent SOC2 Type II evidence for CloudStore and BackupLedger (redacted) and an audit statement for GlacierEdge.

Timeline: Aug 6–8 is doable from our side, but we recommend starting the job outside the 02:00–06:00 maintenance window for BackupLedger (UTC).

One caveat: GlacierEdge has a 14-day quarantine for archived objects after an eviction is triggered (this is the archival provider's policy, we do not automatically override it). If any EU customer needs an exception for a legal hold, that will extend the retention for those objects.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call Monday morning to align across teams.

Best,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Customer Integrations, LogicaCloud
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@logicacloud.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Jul 2028 12:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Ephemeral log eviction protocol and cross-border purge timeline

Thanks Sofia — this is helpful. A couple of internal asks (copying them here so LogicaCloud has visibility):

1) Can you provide the subprocessor contract dates and DPA addenda that reference the 14-day GlacierEdge quarantine? We need an explicit clause for audit and for any customer evidence requests.

2) For EU customers, we need a map of which tenant data may have cross-border replicas (region list + storage class). If CloudStore has any automatic replication to non-EU regions, call that out.

3) Please confirm whether BackupLedger's maintenance window (02:00–06:00 UTC) will block eviction jobs, or if we can queue outside that window. If the job fails mid-run because BackupLedger enters maintenance, we need a failure/fallback path documented.

Internal note to Michael and Kimberly: if GlacierEdge enforces 14 days, we should propose a short-term legal-hold exception flow for customers with active audits (CS to own). Also, update the DPA appendix with a subprocessor-specific timeline table so sales/procurement can set expectations.

-Irene

Subject: Re: Ephemeral log eviction protocol and cross-border purge timeline

Sofia / team —

Appreciate the quick answers and the willingness to run Aug 6–8. Agreed next steps:

- LogicaCloud to share (by Mon COB): subprocessor DPAs/addenda and the storage-region map for cross-border replicas.
- LogicaCloud to confirm whether BackupLedger allows scheduled jobs outside 02:00–06:00 UTC; if not, provide the failure/retry behavior.
- Redwood to draft an appendix to our DPA that lists: subprocessor names, retention-for-eviction (days), and archival quarantine windows. I'll circulate a first pass by EOD Monday.

Attachments: retention-eviction-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal with proposed run order), retention-matrix.xlsx (customer-impact matrix).

Ticket: HubSpot HB-8921 (LogicaCloud purge coordination) — I'll link the Doc with the DPA appendix there.

If you can confirm the distribution list for incident/legal hold notices (who on LogicaCloud to ping if a customer requests pause), we'll lock the schedule.

Thanks — Michael
